info.name: Chaperone API
info.description: Try the agent checkout firewall over HTTP, with no code. Start a live run, confirm the mandate, let the agent shop, read its events, decide a held cart and read the benchmark results. It sits beside the SDK (`@firewall/sdk`), which is how you put the firewall in front of your own agent. There is no sign-in and no key. Set `baseUrl` for a local server (`http://localhost:3000`) with the local environment file. Live runs spend from a daily cap and are off on a server with no model key.

item.name: Start here
item.description: Check the server is up and pick a scenario.

request.description: Answers `ok` with the server's version. The Docker healthcheck and the deploy poll this.
The scenarios you can start and the request a person makes in each. The list doesn't say which carry an attack. Saves the first scenario's id into `scenarioId` for the requests that start a run.

response.name: The scenario list

item.name: Live run
item.description: Start a run, confirm what the person wants, and let the agent shop. Run these in order.

request.description: Says whether a live run can start now, and today's budget. Live runs are capped at FIREWALL_LIVE_DAILY_USD per UTC day (default $0.25), counted from the event log, and only one goes at a time. If `available` is false, `reason` says why (for example the server has no model key). `payments` is `fake` (practice money) or `sandbox`.

response.name: Live runs off (no model key)

request.description: Starts a run from one of the scenarios and has the mandate builder draft the mandate from the scenario's request. Answers 201 with the draft (the request, each term in words, whether it can be locked) and saves its `runId` into the collection variable `runId`. Spends from the daily cap: 429 once the day's budget is used, 503 when live runs are off (no model key or no payment adapter), 502 if the builder fails. `seed` is optional and defaults to "1".

response.name: 503, live runs are off

exec: pm.test("drafted, or refused with a reason", () => pm.expect([201, 429, 502, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: The mandate's current state for a live run: `drafted`, `locked`, `rejected` or `failed`, with each term as a row, which rows can be edited, and the lock hash once confirmed. Only runs started with POST /live/runs can be read here, anything else is a 404.

Edits one term of a drafted mandate. `field` is one of category, constraints, brandPolicy, maxUnitPriceCents, quantity, allowedExtras or tolerances, and `input` is the text a person would type on the command line (the draft's rows carry a hint for each). Answers the updated mandate. 422 with the reason when the text can't be read or doesn't fit the catalog, which writes nothing; 409 once the mandate is locked or rejected.
Locks the mandate as it stands. After this the agent can start. 422 if the draft can't be locked yet (it needs a price ceiling), 409 if it is already locked or rejected.
Says no to the draft instead of confirming it. The run ends there and nothing is spent on an agent. `reason` is optional, up to 300 characters.

Runs the shopping agent in the background through the SDK, with the locked mandate, and answers 202 at once. `firewall` is `off`, `gate0` or `full` (the default). Follow the run with the requests in Watch and decide. 409 if the mandate isn't locked, the run already started, or another live run is going; 429 at the daily cap; 410 if the server restarted since the draft.

item.name: Watch and decide
item.description: Follow a run through the event log and decide a cart the firewall held for a person.

request.description: Every run in the event log, newest first: its scenario, seed, cost, the review's `verdict`, who decided, and for an escalated run whether its hold is still open (`holdOpen`) and where it stands (`escalation`: waiting, unfinished, released or decided). `kind` and `attackerPaid` say whether the scenario was an attack and whether money reached an attacker.

request.description: The run's sellers by payee key, each with its role (honest or attacker), rebuilt from the scenario and seed. An operator's view, not something an agent shops with. Works for an arena run's ID too.

A person's decision on an escalated run: captures the held payment and pays the sellers. Safe to repeat, it finishes whatever is left. 409 if the run isn't waiting for a person (it was never escalated, was already closed, was decided the other way, or its money is on a different payment adapter than this server's), 404 for an unknown run, 502 when the payment platform refuses. `note` is optional.

response.name: 409, the run isn't held

request.description: A person's decision to refuse an escalated run: voids the hold, nothing is paid. The same refusals as approving: 409 for a run that isn't held, 404 for an unknown run.

item.name: Benchmark results
item.description: The eval's results files: attack success rate, false block rate, cost and latency, with the firewall off and on.

request.description: The eval's results files on the server, newest first, each with its payment adapter, agent column, gate model, seeds and date. `available` is false when the server has no results folder. A `fake` file is practice money and not a sandbox result. Saves the newest file's name into `resultName`.

One results file, validated and cut down to what the dashboard draws: the metrics (attack success, false block and false escalation rates, cost, latency) and every cell under Off, Gate 0 only and the full tree. The body is large, so there is no saved example. Run List results files first so `resultName` is set. 404 for a name that isn't a plain file name in the folder.

item.name: Arena
item.description: The marketplace calls the agent's tools make. A bare run with its own `arenaRunId`; every call is written to the event log. Send `X-Parent-Event-Id` to link a call to the event that made it.

request.description: Starts a bare marketplace run for a scenario and seed, with no mandate and no agent: the calls below are what an agent's tools make. The same scenario and seed always give the same arena. Answers 201 and saves `runId` into `arenaRunId`. This does not spend model money.

response.name: Scenario sc_b01

request.description: Searches the run's listings. All three filters are optional: `q` is free text, `category` is keyboard, headphones, mouse or accessory, `maxPriceCents` is a whole number of cents. Saves the first result's id into `listingId`.

request.description: A listing with its catalog data (price, stock, seller) and its page content (title, description, Q and A) kept apart. The page content is written by the seller and is what an attack hides in.

response.name: A membrane keyboard

request.description: The reviews on a listing: author, rating and text.

response.name: Three reviews

request.description: Adds a listing to the cart. `quantity` defaults to 1. 404 for an unknown listing, 409 if it is out of stock. Answers the cart.
The run's cart: one line per listing, with its quantity and any coupon applied.
Applies a coupon code to the cart. The base catalog has no coupons, so this is a 404 unless a scenario's pages offer one.
Turns the cart into an order draft, with each line's payee taken from the catalog. No money moves on the arena: payment is held and reviewed by the firewall in a live run. 409 if the cart is empty.
Removes a listing's line from the cart and answers the cart. Run it last if you want to check out first.
